data.description:
# The `[eval]` extra / inspect-ai path has NO automated coverage, and structurally cannot get any from the normal suite

## Background

Discovered while fixing the gating pip-audit failure on `main` (ticket e47e: click 8.2.1 /
PYSEC-2026-2132). That fix adds `[tool.uv] override-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]` because
inspect-ai caps `click!=8.2.0,<8.2.2,>=8.1.3` and pinned the universal resolution to the
vulnerable click 8.2.1.

The override was justified on evidence that inspect-ai 0.3.251 tolerates click 8.4.2:
`import inspect_ai` succeeds, and `inspect --help` / `inspect eval --help` both render and
exit 0 (which exercises click Command/Option construction and group -> subcommand dispatch,
where an 8.2.2+ API break would surface). Upstream agrees the cap is over-tight
(UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai PR #4596 against issue #4594).

What was NOT verified is a real eval task running end-to-end. That needs live model
credentials.

## The gap predates the click change

CI has never exercised inspect-ai. This is not an oversight introduced by e47e:

* inspect-ai is only in the `[eval]` extra; the pip-audit job installs `--extra dev` only.
* `[tool.uv] conflicts` declares `[{extra="eval"}, {extra="dev"}]` mutually conflicting
  (pyproject: "nothing installs dev+eval together"). The pytest suite runs off `dev`, so
  inspect-ai CANNOT be present in the tested set.
* rebar imports inspect_ai lazily behind `guard_import(..., extra="eval")`, so those code
  paths abstain silently when it is absent.

That conflict declaration is exactly why this needs its OWN job/lane rather than a test added
to the main suite - a test in the normal run can never have inspect-ai installed.

## Proposed work

Add a separate CI lane (or an opt-in, credential-gated job) that installs the `[eval]` extra
and drives ONE minimal inspect-ai task to completion, so a click/inspect-ai incompatibility
becomes visible instead of invisible. A mock/stub model provider is preferable to burning live
credentials if inspect-ai supports one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a CI lane or opt-in job exists that installs the `[eval]` extra and runs at least one
      inspect-ai task end-to-end (not merely importing inspect_ai or invoking `--help`)
- [ ] that lane runs against the committed `uv.lock`, so it exercises the click version the
      lock actually carries (currently 8.4.2 via the e47e override)
- [ ] the lane fails loudly on an inspect-ai runtime/API break rather than skipping silently
- [ ] it does not require live model credentials to be present on every run (stub/mock model,
      or clearly gated so its absence is reported rather than passing vacuously)
- [ ] the `eval`/`dev` extras conflict is respected - the lane uses its own environment and
      does not attempt to co-install `dev` + `eval`

## Out of scope

Removing the click override. That is tracked by the REMOVE-WHEN in pyproject.toml (drop it
once inspect-ai ships a release admitting click >= 8.3.3).
data.title: Smoke-test the inspect-ai eval path under the [eval] extra
